title: Hand hygiene and PPE changes
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate hand hygiene and ppe changes

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Before beginning, identify when hand hygiene is required: on entry where directed, before handling clean supplies, after glove removal, after handling waste, after contamination and at task transitions. Follow the workplace-approved handwashing or hand-rub procedure; visibly dirty hands generally require soap and water. Select gloves and other PPE from the risk assessment, product label and site requirements, not habit alone. Inspect PPE before use, remove it without touching contaminated outer surfaces where possible, dispose or decontaminate it according to policy and perform hand hygiene afterwards. Never reuse single-use gloves.

instruction.heading: Learning focus
instruction.body: Apply hand hygiene and PPE change rules. Before beginning, identify when hand hygiene is required: on entry where directed, before handling clean supplies, after glove removal, after handling waste, after contamination and at task transitions. Follow the workplace-approved handwashing or hand-rub procedure; visibly dirty hands generally require soap and water. Select gloves and other PPE from the risk assessment, product label and site requirements, not habit alone. Inspect PPE before use, remove it without touching contaminated outer surfaces where possible, dispose or decontaminate it according to policy and perform hand hygiene afterwards. Never reuse single-use gloves.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace scenario
instruction.body: A cleaner removes contaminated gloves then opens a clean supply cabinet without cleaning their hands. The instructor demonstrates the missing hygiene step and has the learner repeat the sequence.

instruction.heading: Guided practice
instruction.body: Demonstrate hand hygiene, glove donning and doffing, and a transition from toilet cleaning to a clean supply task without contaminating the clean zone.

instruction.heading: Quality and safety checks
instruction.body: Before signing off, confirm that the method matches the authorised site scope and current product labels, that no uncontrolled hazard remains, and that evidence is factual and privacy-safe.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Identify the hand hygiene points: on entry where directed, before handling clean supplies, after glove removal, after handling waste, after contamination, and at task transitions.
Use the workplace-approved handwashing or hand-rub procedure, and wash with soap and water when hands are visibly dirty.
Select gloves and other PPE from the risk assessment, the product label and the site requirements, not from habit.
Inspect each item of PPE for damage before use.
Remove PPE without touching contaminated outer surfaces where possible.
Dispose of or decontaminate used PPE under policy, and never reuse single-use gloves.
Perform hand hygiene after removing PPE and before handling any clean supply.
If an uncontrolled hazard or unauthorised task appears, stop, keep clear and escalate under the site procedure.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Hands are cleaned at every set point, such as once gloves come off and whenever the task changes.
Visibly dirty hands are washed with soap and water, using the workplace procedure.
Each protective item is checked prior to use and matched to the hazard review, product label and site rules.
Contaminated gloves are removed and disposed of before any clean supply is handled.
summary: Hand hygiene is needed on entry where directed, before handling clean supplies, after glove removal and waste handling, and at task transitions.
Gloves and other protective equipment are picked against the task risk review, the manufacturer's label and the site rules, then checked for damage before each use.
Used PPE is removed without touching contaminated outer surfaces, disposed of or decontaminated under policy, and followed by hand hygiene.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked when changing PPE between rooms?
options: Only that the gloves are a bright colour and that they fit the hand and the wrist
That the PPE selection matches the risk assessment, product label and site requirements
That single-use gloves can be reused for a second room if they look clean enough
That the usual habit of wearing gloves is still right for every job in every room

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a hazard found during a glove change be handled?
options: Stop, keep clear of the hazard, and escalate per the site procedure
Continue, since hand hygiene solves any problem and the gloves are changed
Remove gloves, wash hands and carry on with the same task
Reuse single-use gloves until the hazard is cleared and then wash them

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say hand hygiene is required?
options: Only at the end of the job
Only if the hands look visibly clean
